newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt investors to sell 30 pct of new cement firm.
newsitem.headline: Egypt investors to sell 30 pct of new cement firm.

text.p: Egyptian investors said on Thursday they would offer 30 percent of a new cement company in southern Egypt for sale to the public.

The company, South Valley Cement Company (SVCC) has an issued capital of 350 million pounds ($100 million) with total investments of 850 million, said the main founders, the Egyptian Saudi Group for South Valley Projects.
SVCC will have a production capacity of 1.4 million tonnes a year in the first stage, the founders said in an announcement.
They said the new plant would be set up in the Western Desert oasis of Kharga, some 550 km(340 miles) southwest of Cairo.
No details of the public offer were published but industry sources told Reuters that the share price would be 10 pounds ($3) and the minimum subscription 1,000 shares.
"The public offer is planned to start within almost a month, with the group and Banque Misr holding 70 percent of the new firm," one of the sources said.
Banque Misr is also acting as agent for the founders in the share offer, the founders said.

The cement plant would be well placed to supply construction sites associated with President Hosni Mubarak's scheme to irrigate at least 500,000 acres of land in the Western desert with water pumped in from the lake behind the Aswan High Dam.
Two other cement companies have recently said they will build plants, one of them in south Egypt.
The cement sector is highly profitable in Egypt and cement firms are among the blue chips on the stock market.
